# QuantScoreCircles

Several inputs converging on a few scores.

## When to use it

Three or four scores on a common scale, shown as derived from named inputs rather than asserted.

## Shape

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | D-quantitative |
| Form | score-circles |
| Arity | 4 |
| Ground | cream, navy |
| Density | dense, about 760 characters |
| Media | none |
| Focal | value at 104px against a 64px headline (ratio 1.63) |

## Why it holds together

The scores dominate, as they should — but all four equally, because none of them is the answer on its own.

## Deviations from the traced source

| What | Source | Here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| my own index note | SELECCION-25-indice.md says to size diameters by the square root of the value | equal diameters | Right instinct, wrong slide. Square-root sizing makes AREA read as magnitude across orders of magnitude; across 85-99 it produces a 7.6% difference that is invisible as data and visible as sloppiness, and it implies the discs are a chart when they are four printed scores. Recorded rather than silently ignored. |

## What the consumer supplies

Copy only. The geometry is measured off a real slide, so when you rebuild it in Claude Design Slides keep the positions and sizes in the preview exactly: change the words, not the grid. Build the text and shapes from the Elements cards, each of which ends with its Slides recipe.

## Origin

Traced from `bank:189` and shipped as canon template `quant-score-circles`. In the repository its template, `wpp-es-html-deck/canon/templates/quant-score-circles.html`, is refreshed from this card's preview, and its trace sources (spec, measurements and reference image) are in `authoring/canon-src/quant-score-circles/`.

# QuantStatGrid5

Claim held up by five numbers across a rule.

## When to use it

A claim needing five pieces of quantitative proof, where the claim is what the room should leave with.

## Shape

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | D-quantitative (secondary A-narrative) |
| Form | kpi-grid |
| Arity | 5 |
| Ground | cream |
| Density | standard, about 720 characters |
| Media | none |
| Focal | value at 132px against a 64px headline (ratio 2.06) |

## Why it holds together

The numerals dominate, but the claim at 64px holds its own — which is why the claim is set at display weight rather than as a 40px headline. Drop the claim to headline size and the slide becomes a stat dump.

## Related kit layout

`StatsV1` — StatsV1 lines four numerals in one row over a ruler and leaves the middle of the canvas empty. This wraps five numbers around a claim and fills. Do not retire StatsV1 until this has been through a real deck.

## Deviations from the traced source

| What | Source | Here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| background texture | dot field | none | The source carries a faint full-bleed dot texture. Reproducing it is a §5 dot-system decision affecting every slide's ground, not a template one. |
| background density | 0.87 background in the y432-990 band | 0.92 | The source carries a full-bleed dot texture this template does not reproduce (a §5 dot-system decision, not a template one). The composition check reads that texture as ink, so it FAILs here and passes there. Not a dead lower half — measured, and the gap is the texture. |

## What the consumer supplies

Copy only. The geometry is measured off a real slide, so when you rebuild it in Claude Design Slides keep the positions and sizes in the preview exactly: change the words, not the grid. Build the text and shapes from the Elements cards, each of which ends with its Slides recipe.

## Origin
